prompt:
Create a NEW original hand-drawn portrait illustration of Jackie Leven around 1971, based ONLY on the two supplied historical PHOTOGRAPHS. Do not reuse, imitate or edit any previously generated portrait.

Input roles: Photo 1 is the primary reference for his facial likeness: long centre-parted hair, a young natural face, thick slightly asymmetric eyebrows, distinctive straight nose, narrow moustache and a small chin beard, reserved expression. Photo 2 supports facial structure and the very long hair. The printed page, text, photographic poses and backgrounds are not part of the illustration.

Art direction: a raw, confident artist's DRAWING, pale charcoal / grey Conté and sparing dry-brush ink on a near-black ground. It must visibly feel made by a moving hand. The likeness is carried by loose, varied marks, not by an accurately shaded photographic surface. Use expressive searching lines, irregular patches of hatching following the facial form, occasional rubbed broadside charcoal strokes, broken outlines, and open unworked areas. A few lively overlapping strokes describe a cheek or temple. Some marks stop abruptly; others trail off. Allow asymmetry and natural variation in the mark-making while keeping the facial anatomy faithful. Details are selective: eyes, nose and mouth are clearly and accurately drawn, while much of the rest is only suggested. The face is drawn, not a realistic face underneath a texture filter.
Hair: a handful of long, freely swept charcoal strokes and loose ink gestures describe the centre part and flowing hair over his shoulders. Large areas of hair remain unworked darkness. No rendering of individual hair strands. Beard: a few short directional strokes. Clothing: sparse gestural lines suggesting an open-collar shirt, shoulders unfinished and disappearing.
Composition: vertical 4:5 head-and-shoulders portrait; whole head visible, long hair flowing down past the shoulders. New natural pose, torso slightly turned, head nearly frontal and eyes looking a little toward the viewer's right. Hands outside the picture, no hand touching the face. A quiet, alert, independent young man, not smiling. Preserve the photographed distinctive facial proportions; do not prettify or substitute a generic rock-star face.
For a dark homage website: background flat deep anthracite #0d0f12, subdued dark and middle greys only. Pale marks are muted grey, never dazzling white. The drawing fades out toward all edges into the dark ground, like a restrained watermark. No visible rectangular sheet or paper border.
Crucial avoid list: NO photorealistic rendering, NO digital painting, NO posterized filter, NO polygonal or vector-like tone shapes, NO smooth gradient modelling, NO glossy impasto, NO embossed/pebbled all-over skin texture, NO uniform decorative noise, NO traced photograph with texture laid on top. Do not over-finish. Keep the spontaneous, economical and imperfect physical feeling of a strong charcoal sketch. No words, lettering, signature, logos, extra people, instruments or background objects.
